acceptanceCriteria: A holder can bind a second ticket's attempt to an allocation it already holds (claim --pool P --share-allocation ID or an equivalent verb); the binding is recorded in receipts, pool occupancy and attempt show.
The member stays ALLOCATED until the last bound attempt releases and is quarantined once per batch, not once per ticket.
Fencing: a bound attempt's lease cannot outlive the allocation; releasing the holder with attempts still bound is refused or hands the allocation over, as the spec states.
Sharing is bounded (a maximum number of attempts per allocation) and refuses foreign holders, other pools and stale allocations with stable codes.
Maintained tests cover bind, ordered and reversed release, refusal paths, crash recovery and journal replay.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#653 (owner: get the new GitHub issues fixed and merged).

Observed (Flow-Proof, 2026-10-07): each flow session claims a pooled lane, prepares it (image refresh, health, global setup: 4-5 min), runs one flow's tests and releases it; release quarantines the lane, which needs a 1-3 min cleanup reset. 97 flow sessions in 24 h paid this separately, about 11 of 96 lane-hours plus orientation tokens. The workaround claims extra tickets without --pool and records the shared allocation only as status text, so the queue cannot audit which allocation ticket B used.

Ask: a supported way for one holder to run several tickets on one allocation, with auditable binding, one quarantine per batch, and fencing.
